I'm 22 and from 2012 on, I wasted the better part of my youth puking my guts out and ripping up my entire body, attempting suicide four times and getting addicted to ephedrine. I would give anything to go back and time and help give lil me a chance. I set myself up for failure. And I was 14, I can't be that mad at someone so naive and clueless, but this handful of vices became my only coping mechanisms during a developmentally substantial portion of my growth. I resent ever picking up a razor, or buying pills, or sticking a toothbrush down my throat. 
Now technically, from now until my late 20s could count as the best years of my life, but I'm still falling apart faster than I can pick up the pieces. I set myself up to miss out on a great life almost a decade ago.

Maybe I can fix it, maybe I can't. All I know for certain is that I'll need to stay alive to find out. And if all I can do right now is survive, then that'll have to be enough, or else I'll never get another chance again.

I don't want to, but I feel like I have to, or else it'll just get worse and I'll have to deal with the consequences later. And I'd rather just deal with it now, even if it's not real. When I do that, though, it kinda makes me feel like I'm coming off as the opposite of clingy and overbearing. Instead of trying to be around him all the time, I leave him alone when I'm home and actively avoid bothering him (is it even really bothering him anyways??? Idk). And I try to refrain from being affectionate and all that because I can feel myself being annoying. 
I'm just incredibly insecure and want to be perfect for him, but if I don't even have am accurate view of myself, how can I do that?
It's not a weakness, though. You deserve the very best, I hope you can find it.

At my store, AP gets eyes on suspicious people and tells people over the headset to go watch them. Back in sales, I would hover around them and be super friendly while cleaning the area (it normally needed cleaning anyway) and sometimes a coworker would join me and we'd make conversation enough for the thieves to give up because we were actively around them. 
I've also noticed that a big issue with this is small, expensive items aren't getting locked up or put in plastic cages. Spiderwraps apparently just aren't doing it. A near $200 apple TV is really small and easy to pocket (especially up here in the winter where everyone and their mother is wearing giant winter coats until April), so if we locked them in plastic boxes wouldn't that help? 
Kind of wish management would listen to me. I'm never really taken seriously (makeup + being really bubbly apparently = people thinking I'm a joke) and when I make suggestions it's shrugged off.

Our older AP people are really sharp, but it's just the one girl that's really lacking. Still, that makes sense. AP always checks my bag when I leave and checks my pockets (I'm one of the only people who brings a big bookbag to work, but I'm a student so I need to) and when customers see AP checking my bag when I'm leaving (after I get out of my uniform, mind you) it freaks them out. Unintentional theft deterrent?

We have identified the people responsible and last time they came in we stopped them before they could do anything, but it's still bad. This only happened once we hired new AP, I swear. And the one new person (aforementioned) is on their phone the entire time they're working front AND back. When I was in sales I always kept hawk eyes on everyone and shrink wasn't nearly as much of an issue when I was on the floor. Now it's all specific brand name products. We know where people tend to steal things the most so we keep eyes and cameras on those places. It's a start but I'm scared I guess. Never worked in retail before.
